question.worked_solution:
The integral is defined over a type II region.

First, we evaluate the inner integral by integrating with respect to $x$, treating $y$ as a constant:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{-2}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{\sqrt{4-{y}^{2}}}3x\,dx\,dy & ={\int }_{-2}^{2}[{\int }_{0}^{\sqrt{4-{y}^{2}}}3x\,dx]dy \\  & ={\int }_{-2}^{2}{[\frac{3}{2}{x}^{2}]}_{0}^{\sqrt{4-{y}^{2}}}\,dy \\  & ={\int }_{-2}^{2}\frac{3}{2}(4-{y}^{2})\,dy \\  & =\frac{3}{2}{\int }_{-2}^{2}(4-{y}^{2})\,dy\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we integrate with respect to $y:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{3}{2}{\int }_{-2}^{2}(4-{y}^{2})\,dy & =\frac{3}{2}\cdot 2{\int }_{0}^{2}(4-{y}^{2})\,dy \\  & =3{\int }_{0}^{2}(4-{y}^{2})\,dy \\  & =3{[4y-\frac{1}{3}{y}^{3}]}_{0}^{2} \\  & =3(8-\frac{8}{3}) \\  & =3(\frac{16}{3}) \\  & =16\end{aligned}
$$
